draft.title: Density
card: Density is how much mass is packed into a given volume. Density = mass ÷ volume, so it is often measured in g/cm³.
The more closely particles are packed, the more particles fit in the same volume, so the more mass there is. Solids are usually denser than liquids, and liquids are usually denser than gases.
Water has a density of about 1 g/cm³. An object with a density lower than the liquid it is in floats. An object with a higher density sinks.
Example: a block with a mass of 200 g and a volume of 50 cm³ has a density of 200 ÷ 50 = 4 g/cm³.
draft.remember: Density = mass ÷ volume. Less dense than the liquid means it floats.

a.q: A metal block has a mass of 300 g and a volume of 100 cm³. What is its density?
opts: 3 g/cm³
0.33 g/cm³
30 g/cm³
400 g/cm³
a.why: Density = mass ÷ volume = 300 ÷ 100 = 3 g/cm³. Dividing volume by mass gives 0.33, which is the wrong way round.
a.clue: Mass goes on the top of the division.

b.q: Mia drops a wax ball with a density of 0.9 g/cm³ into a tank of water. What happens, and why?
opts: It floats, because it is less dense than water
It sinks, because it is less dense than water
It floats, because it is more dense than water
It sinks, because it is more dense than water
b.why: Water has a density of about 1 g/cm³. The wax is less dense than the water, so it floats. The option that says it sinks has the right comparison but the wrong result.
b.clue: Compare 0.9 with the density of water.

b.best: It floats, because it is less dense than water

problems.detail: The why says 'The option that says it sinks has the right comparison but the wrong result', but two options say it sinks. Only 'It sinks, because it is less dense than water' has the right comparison, so the sentence is ambiguous.

check.summary: The card and both questions are correct. One small problem: the why for (b) refers to 'the option that says it sinks' when two options say it sinks, so it should name the one meant.
